81353.subject: Clarification: Recent API key revocations are precautionary
81353.body:
Railway Logo

Railway is stable and operational, and not currently under attack. The October 21st incident is resolved, however, you may have seen API key revocations from OpenAI or see further API key revocations from other API providers.

Here’s what happened:

* October 22 at 03:32 UTC: We confirmed the attacker no longer had access to our internal systems, as documented in our preliminary report ( https://blog.railway.com/p/preliminary-report-october-security-incident?utm_campaign=AI+Provider+Key+Revocations+%E2%80%94+Clarification+%E2%80%94+2026-10-24&utm_content=AI+Provider+Key+Revocations+%E2%80%94+Clarification+%E2%80%94+2026-10-24&utm_medium=email_action&utm_source=customer.io ). We have no further evidence of compromise since then.
* October 23: AI providers requested another batch of potentially affected keys.
* October 24 at approximately 04:43 UTC: We provided OpenAI and Anthropic with key hashes. Because we could not filter keys by when they were added, the batch inadvertently included hashes of newer keys.
* Providers subsequently revoked keys as a precaution, we know OpenAI revoked keys potentially including replacements you created after the incident. Other providers may revoke keys in that list. These revocations do not indicate that your replacement keys were compromised.

You should also receive communications directly from the providers taking action, explaining their response and any steps you need to take.

If a provider revoked your key:

* Create a replacement key with that provider.
* Update the corresponding Railway environment variable.
* Redeploy the services that use it.

If your keys are still working, this notice does not require you to repeat completed rotations. We’re sorry for the confusion and additional disruption. For help restoring service, contact support@railway.com ( support@railway.com?utm_campaign=AI+Provider+Key+Revocations+%E2%80%94+Clarification+%E2%80%94+2026-10-24&utm_content=AI+Provider+Key+Revocations+%E2%80%94+Clarification+%E2%80%94+2026-10-24&utm_medium=email_action&utm_source=customer.io ).

Thanks,
The Railway Team

Unsubscribe from marketing emails ( https://railway.com/preferences?token=4c2e4edf-bffd-4b7a-ad7d-a802198020ea&utm_campaign=AI+Provider+Key+Revocations+%E2%80%94+Clarification+%E2%80%94+2026-10-24&utm_content=AI+Provider+Key+Revocations+%E2%80%94+Clarification+%E2%80%94+2026-10-24&utm_medium=email_action&utm_source=customer.io )

80931.subject: Team1 Japan: Institutions Chose Avalanche. Now It’s the Builders’ Turn.
80931.body:
View this post on the web at https://www.team1.blog/p/team1-japan-institutions-chose-avalanche

Team1 Japan is officially here.
Our mission is to build a Japanese builder community that matches the scale of Japan’s institutional adoption.
Here is what that means, and why Japan’s builder scene is unique.
The sequence is backwards, and that’s the opportunity
Japan’s institutions have already made their choice.
Progmat, the platform behind the majority of the country’s security token issuance, moved billions in tokenized real estate and corporate bonds onto a dedicated Avalanche L1. TIS, which processes more than half of Japan’s credit card volume, also launched its own L1. Some of the largest names in Japanese finance are now exploring tokenized government bonds using Avalanche infrastructure.
In most countries, this runs the other way. A community forms, developers experiment, projects ship, and eventually, sometimes years later, institutions notice and follow. Japan skipped the first half.
The chains themselves stay controlled, as Japanese financial regulation requires, but they no longer sit behind a wall. Gateways outward to wallets, to stablecoin settlement, and to applications written by people who were never invited into a private consortium are now being built. Japan’s financial system is no longer a closed circuit. It is growing an edge you can build against.
The demand is real, and the gateways to these platforms are underway.
That’s the gap Team1 Japan is here to close.
Want to keep up with the latest in the Avalanche ecosystem? Subscribe to the Team1 blog and get our updates in your inbox weekly.
What is Team1?
Team1 is a network of builders, developers, creators, event organizers, and community leaders working to grow the Avalanche ecosystem from the ground up. Since launching in 2024, it has grown to hundreds of members across more than 40 countries, with official chapters now live in the USA, Vietnam, India, Türkiye, Brasil, and across LatAm.
Team1 Japan is the newest of those chapters.
Our mandate is focused: connect Japan’s builders to Avalanche, and connect them to each other.
This is a formalization, not a beginning
Japan’s Avalanche community has been meeting for years.
Since April 2023, over 30 events have been held across Tokyo, Osaka, Nagoya, and Fukuoka with more than 1200 attendees between them. The anchor is Avalanche Gourmet Night, a series running for over two years that marks the beginning of the Avalanche community’s in-person presence
The programming has widened past meetups. Avalanche Academy study sessions have run four times since March, giving developers a recurring technical space rather than a social one. There have been collaborations with Uniswap Labs, zeroone, and Pudgy Penguins, and a workshop for teams who entered the JPYC stablecoin innovation challenge.

80805.subject: More Trading, Different Activity: Avalanche’s Latest 30 Days
80805.body:
View this post on the web at https://www.team1.blog/p/more-trading-different-activity-avalanches

Nansen recorded 48.4 million transactions, down 33% from the previous 30 days. At the same time, DEX volume climbed to $2.7 billion, up 145%, while active users increased 8.1% to 1.6 million.
So Avalanche was not simply quieter. There were fewer transactions in Nansen’s dataset, but much more trading volume. Users still grew, capital continued moving through the ecosystem, and activity across individual Avalanche L1s adds another part of the picture.
Trading picked up fast
The biggest change is DEX volume. WAVAX alone accounted for around $2.5 billion, with roughly $1.3 billion in buys and $1.3 billion in sells.
Active users also moved higher, reaching around 1.6 million, up 8.1% from the previous period. If that user growth continues while transactions stabilize, this month may end up looking more like a change in how Avalanche is being used than a simple drop in activity.
Want to keep up with the latest in the Avalanche ecosystem? Subscribe to the Team1 blog and get our updates in your inbox weekly.
AVAX and WAVAX are moving differently
Around $4.6 million of native AVAX left exchange wallets over the latest seven days. WAVAX went the other way. Around $12.3 million moved into exchanges, while Top PnL wallets reduced their WAVAX positions by roughly $2.2 million.
Native AVAX is moving away from exchanges while WAVAX is moving toward them. At the same time, WAVAX remains extremely active on DEXs. For now, it looks more like capital moving around the ecosystem than everyone taking the same position.
Fresh wallets are still bringing money in
Fresh wallets added approximately $20.8 million in AVAX over seven days. Another $16.3 million went into WAVAX. Those are meaningful inflows, but both were below their normal levels. AVAX was running at around 0.6x its average flow, while WAVAX was around 0.4x.
New wallets are participating, just not at an unusually high rate. There is fresh capital coming in, but this does not look like another sudden wave of adoption.
BTC.b is still doing real volume
BTC.b continues to be one of the more active parts of Avalanche DeFi. It recorded around $238.8 million in DEX volume over 30 days, with approximately $1.3 million in net flow.
Over the latest seven days, BTC.b generated another $60.9 million in volume, with $31.5 million in buys and $29.4 million in sells.
There is no major imbalance between buyers and sellers. It is simply an active market.
Bitcoin liquidity gives Avalanche another source of capital beyond AVAX and stablecoins, and BTC.b is still moving through the ecosystem rather than simply sitting in wallets.
sAVAX looks steady
sAVAX has around 16,609 holders, approximately $169.8 million in market cap, and roughly $2.2 million in liquidity. Seven-day volume was around $743,000, with approximately $424,000 in buys compared with $319,000 in sells.
There is no obvious new staking surge here.
